candidate_denominator.hypothesis: Stocks with high 5-day simple returns accompanied by positive volume changes tend to exhibit short-term overreaction and subsequently underperform; the factor is the negative bounded interaction so higher values select less overbought stocks.

When same-day return and volume change point in the same direction, order flow is more likely informed and should persist cross-sectionally; opposite signs indicate volume-price divergence. The bounded interaction avoids extreme-volume dominance.

Stocks with accelerating volume changes may attract market attention and experience short-term continuation; the difference between recent and longer-volume changes, bounded via arctangent, provides an economically interpretable A-share cross-sectional signal.

When the 1-day return is high relative to the prior 5-day return, short-term overreaction tends to reverse, so stocks with high positive spread underperform subsequently; the bounded ratio provides a stable, low-turnover signal complementary to volume-based factors.

Stocks with simultaneously elevated turnover and large absolute 5-day volume changes attract speculative attention and subsequently underperform; therefore the negative product should be positively related to future returns.

Stocks with current turnover far above their trailing 20-day average experience short-term attention-driven overpricing, leading to lower forward returns; the factor is bounded via arctan and requires at least five valid turnover observations.
